title.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire Investment for Growth DPF3/PBG/D4D

description.narrative: The Program Development Objective (PDO) of the proposed operation is to: (1) strengthen competition in key enabling sectors and domestic revenue mobilization; (2) expand equitable access to health and education services; (3) promote the sustainable use of natural resources.

The development objective of Third Investment for Growth Development Policy Financing Project for Côte d'Ivoire is to: (1) strengthen competition in key enabling sectors and domestic revenue mobilization; (2) expand equitable access to health and education services; (3) promote the sustainable use of natural resources. In December 2021, Côte d’Ivoire adopted the National Development Plan (PND) 2021-2025, as its main strategic planning document to sustain high economic growth and inclusion in the medium-term. This operation directly supports the first three categories of actions of the PND and is aligned with the country's climate change commitments and the Paris Agreement. The operation also supports outcome area four of the new corporate score card: effective macroeconomic and fiscal management. By improving tax revenue collection, it supports a stable fiscal environment that can help government manage debt and marshal resources to deliver services such as health, education, and infrastructure. The operation has three pillars: Pillar 1: Strengthen competition in key enabling sectors and domestic revenue mobilization; Pillar 2: Expand equitable access to health and education services; and Pillar 3: Promote the sustainable use of natural resources.

title.narrative: 2. Share of national freight transactions carried out through the freight exchange

comment.narrative: The implementation faces challenges. While the Protocol of Agreement between the Ministry of Transport and the Office Ivoire des Chargeurs has been signed, the implementation of the Freight Exchange platform is pending due to the awaited application texts of Ordinance No. 2023-718. These texts are crucial for ARTI to effectively monitor and control the platform's operations, including enforcement powers. Additionally, collaboration among ARTI, DGTTC, and OIC is essential to achieve the target of 40,000 tons by 2026. Upcoming steps include setting freight transport tariffs and financial penalties, and officially designating ARTI as the regulatory authority.

title.narrative: 1a. Financial service providers using USSD codes (number)

comment.narrative: Odds seem favorable to reach the target by December 2025. Yet, BCEA is tightetning regulation on fintech companies, requiring that only licensed entities can provide digital payment services in the WAEMU region. This initiative aims to improve consumer protection, ensurefinancial stability, and standardize operations across the region. Smaller firms that cannot meet the compliance standards will be unable to obtain a license to operate. In this case, the indicator could be impacted negatively.

title.narrative: 1b. Retail prices for telecommunications services (price of a data-only 2GB mobile-broadband basket as share of Gross National Income (GNI) per capita)

comment.narrative: As of June 2025, the price of a 2GB mobile-broadband basket is 1.89% of GNI per capita. This figure is below the global target of 2% and brings us very close to the DPO affordability target of 1.80% by December 2025. The target is well within reach, and ITU is expected to release new data this summer. [Data dashboard: https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Statistics/Dashboards/Pages/IPB.aspx]

title.narrative: 7. Cocoa traced and compliant with sustainability standards (percentage of total cocoa exported per season)

comment.narrative: Despite 85% of producers having cards to track 60% of production, progress is slow because paper-based field purchases are still common. To tackle this, Côte d'Ivoire plans to require digital purchases by October 1, 2025, postponing the original deadline of October 1, 2024. Although this change will enhance the indicator, it may still fall short of the target by the end of 2025.

title.narrative: 8b: Hectares of agroforests with signed concession agreements

comment.narrative: Implementation is underway. The Government–Adryada agreement approved by the Council of Ministers in December 2025 (EUR 120 million to rehabilitate 104,000 ha of the Haut Sassandra Gazetted Forests). MINEF plans to replicate a government led approach for FIP2 targeted forests, which already have approved management plans, leveraging prior negotiations to accelerate implementation.

title.narrative: 7. Cocoa traced and compliant with sustainability standards (percentage of total cocoa exported per season)

comment.narrative: The original target to eliminate paper transactions by October 1, 2025 has not been achieved given the postponement of the EU DR implementation by the EU. However, since the start of the October cocoa campaign, operators have shown a strong commitment to adopt the digital cocoa traceability system, with approximately 50,000 tons marketed through the platform. While this marks progress, it is still below the target.

title.narrative: 8a: Hectares of forests classified as agroforests

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The first three nationwide agroforests, supported by the FIP2, encompass a total of 548,000 hectares and include Scio, Rapides Grah, and Haute-Dodo. These three forests have been officially designated as agroforests and have an agroforest management plan that has been approved by decree.

title.narrative: 9: Urban coastal areas protected by climate and risk informed local urban plans (percentage)

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Within the WACA project the following climate and risk informed local urban plans were developed; (i) as part of the Integrated Coastal Development and Management Plan (PAGIL) (June 2022) , a climate and risk informed local urban development plan was developed for Grand BEreby; (ii) the Grand Lahou urban development plan (Agenda 21) was also developed and validated in December 2024; (iii) the Coastal and Maritime Spatial Planning of the municipality of Assinie was finalized in July 2024.

title.narrative: 3. Tax revenue to GDP ratio (3-year average) (percentage)

comment.narrative: The government has intensified its tax reforms, guided by the Medium-Term Revenue Strategy (MTRS). These reforms, also supported by the SDFP FY24 and FY25, have enabled the country to meet all its revenue performance criteria (PPAs). Tax revenue is projected to reach 15 percent of GDP by 2025. Further support for these reforms was provided by the IMF program.
